overview: 105 approved publications: 47 randomized trial reports, 42 reviews or syntheses, eight qualitative studies and eight observational studies. They comprise 100 additions and five existing-library matches. The 47 randomized reports represent 42 conservatively linked trial units. Cross-listed papers and institutional groups overlap; publication counts are not independent participants or trials.
limitations: AI assessed; human approved for publication. This rapid review inspected selected methods and retained source evidence; it is not an independent systematic risk-of-bias or GRADE assessment. Age ranges often extend below 16 or above 24. Source access, age fit, masking, attrition and transfer limits remain attached to each paper. Article crosses describe study design, not benefit, certainty or human clinical review. Reviews do not inherit the crosses of their included trials.
labFraming: The Universal Mind Mobile Lab is planned as an education and creative-skills initiative: electronic music, fashion and mindfulness experiences, stigma reduction and referral pathways. Reduced short-term stress and greater felt connection are exploratory outcomes to measure. No included paper tests the combined lab model.

Direct response means a response to a documented need or access barrier. Inspired by means a design or evaluation idea informed by relevant research. Neither label establishes that the proposed lab will reproduce a study outcome. Null findings and limits are included alongside supportive evidence.

Ben has identified Central Coast, Bondi / Bondi Junction and Northern Rivers near Byron Bay as the first three destinations. Permanent sites depend on community and council agreement. Public self-nomination, touring and smaller pop-ups are planned access routes. Headspace, Black Dog Institute and Orygen are prospective partners; no partnership or endorsement is asserted.

Programme planning includes youth co-design, community authority, mentoring for 16–17-year-olds, separate clinical referral and nonclinical learning pathways, and independent choices about research and filming. Continuity after a visit, referral follow-through, affordability, transport, accessibility and culturally governed participation remain practical design and evaluation questions.

evidence.text: Trauma-focused treatments for refugee children and adolescents with PTSD: a three-arm randomized controlled trial comparing the efficacy of EMDR and KIDNET versus a waitlist control group (the KIEM study).

records.authors: Zheng S, Shen Y, Geng F, Ye M, Song S, Wang R, Zhang S, Ou Y, Zhou X.

sound.title: AI Guided Youth Research
overview: 105 approved publications: 47 randomized trial reports, 42 reviews or syntheses, eight qualitative studies and eight observational studies. They comprise 100 additions and five existing-library matches. The 47 randomized reports represent 42 conservatively linked trial units. Cross-listed papers and institutional groups overlap; publication counts are not independent participants or trials.

AI assessed; human approved for publication. This rapid review inspected selected methods and retained source evidence; it is not an independent systematic risk-of-bias or GRADE assessment. Age ranges often extend below 16 or above 24. Source access, age fit, masking, attrition and transfer limits remain attached to each paper. Article crosses describe study design, not benefit, certainty or human clinical review. Reviews do not inherit the crosses of their included trials.

topics.title: Universal Mind Mobile Lab · Direct response and inspired by
topics.description: 11 publications in Sound; cross-listing is not additional evidence. Reported ages and source limits remain visible in each record.
paragraphs: Chapter Trust Factor counts distinct qualifying study families. Paper crosses identify each publication’s design. Neither score establishes effectiveness; related reports and overlapping reviews are not independent replications.

The Universal Mind Mobile Lab is planned as an education and creative-skills initiative: electronic music, fashion and mindfulness experiences, stigma reduction and referral pathways. Reduced short-term stress and greater felt connection are exploratory outcomes to measure. No included paper tests the combined lab model.

Direct response means a response to a documented need or access barrier. Inspired by means a design or evaluation idea informed by relevant research. Neither label establishes that the proposed lab will reproduce a study outcome. Null findings and limits are included alongside supportive evidence.

Ben has identified Central Coast, Bondi / Bondi Junction and Northern Rivers near Byron Bay as the first three destinations. Permanent sites depend on community and council agreement. Public self-nomination, touring and smaller pop-ups are planned access routes. Headspace, Black Dog Institute and Orygen are prospective partners; no partnership or endorsement is asserted.

Programme planning includes youth co-design, community authority, mentoring for 16–17-year-olds, separate clinical referral and nonclinical learning pathways, and independent choices about research and filming. Continuity after a visit, referral follow-through, affordability, transport, accessibility and culturally governed participation remain practical design and evaluation questions.

trustAssessment.basis: Existing minimum-three-study design rubric. Known linked reports count once by trial unit or study family. Overlap between reviews remains a limitation; no pooled efficacy or certainty grade is assigned.

topics.title: Universal Mind Mobile Lab · Direct response and inspired by
topics.description: 7 publications in Vision; cross-listing is not additional evidence. Reported ages and source limits remain visible in each record.
paragraphs: Chapter Trust Factor counts distinct qualifying study families. Paper crosses identify each publication’s design. Neither score establishes effectiveness; related reports and overlapping reviews are not independent replications.

The Universal Mind Mobile Lab is planned as an education and creative-skills initiative: electronic music, fashion and mindfulness experiences, stigma reduction and referral pathways. Reduced short-term stress and greater felt connection are exploratory outcomes to measure. No included paper tests the combined lab model.

Direct response means a response to a documented need or access barrier. Inspired by means a design or evaluation idea informed by relevant research. Neither label establishes that the proposed lab will reproduce a study outcome. Null findings and limits are included alongside supportive evidence.

Ben has identified Central Coast, Bondi / Bondi Junction and Northern Rivers near Byron Bay as the first three destinations. Permanent sites depend on community and council agreement. Public self-nomination, touring and smaller pop-ups are planned access routes. Headspace, Black Dog Institute and Orygen are prospective partners; no partnership or endorsement is asserted.

Programme planning includes youth co-design, community authority, mentoring for 16–17-year-olds, separate clinical referral and nonclinical learning pathways, and independent choices about research and filming. Continuity after a visit, referral follow-through, affordability, transport, accessibility and culturally governed participation remain practical design and evaluation questions.

overview: 105 approved publications: 47 randomized trial reports, 42 reviews or syntheses, eight qualitative studies and eight observational studies. AI assessed; human approved for publication. This rapid review inspected selected methods and retained source evidence; it is not an independent systematic risk-of-bias or GRADE assessment. Age ranges often extend below 16 or above 24. Source access, age fit, masking, attrition and transfer limits remain attached to each paper. topics.title: Universal Mind Mobile Lab · Direct response and inspired by
topics.description: 89 publications in Language; cross-listing is not additional evidence. Reported ages and source limits remain visible in each record.
paragraphs: Chapter Trust Factor counts distinct qualifying study families. Paper crosses identify each publication’s design. Neither score establishes effectiveness; related reports and overlapping reviews are not independent replications.

The Universal Mind Mobile Lab is planned as an education and creative-skills initiative: electronic music, fashion and mindfulness experiences, stigma reduction and referral pathways. Reduced short-term stress and greater felt connection are exploratory outcomes to measure. No included paper tests the combined lab model.

Direct response means a response to a documented need or access barrier. Inspired by means a design or evaluation idea informed by relevant research. Neither label establishes that the proposed lab will reproduce a study outcome. Null findings and limits are included alongside supportive evidence.

Ben has identified Central Coast, Bondi / Bondi Junction and Northern Rivers near Byron Bay as the first three destinations. Permanent sites depend on community and council agreement. Public self-nomination, touring and smaller pop-ups are planned access routes. Headspace, Black Dog Institute and Orygen are prospective partners; no partnership or endorsement is asserted.

Programme planning includes youth co-design, community authority, mentoring for 16–17-year-olds, separate clinical referral and nonclinical learning pathways, and independent choices about research and filming. Continuity after a visit, referral follow-through, affordability, transport, accessibility and culturally governed participation remain practical design and evaluation questions.

trustAssessment.basis: Existing minimum-three-study design rubric. Known linked reports count once by trial unit or study family. Overlap between reviews remains a limitation; no pooled efficacy or certainty grade is assigned.
